overview: This Senate resolution supports naming April 2026 "National Child Abuse Prevention Month." It cites figures on how many children are reported to child protective services each year and how common child abuse, neglect, and sexual abuse are, and describes the lasting health effects of harmful childhood experiences. It points to voluntary home-visiting programs, in which trained workers support new and expecting parents, as having reduced repeat abuse and improved children's outcomes. The resolution supports public education on preventing abuse, efforts to help survivors heal, and justice for victims. It is symbolic and does not create any program or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 14, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution raises awareness that child abuse is preventable and backs proven approaches to protect children and support families.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide funding for prevention programs or survivor services.
